credit_line: Terrain made from NASA data: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation models from NASA Goddard's Planetary Geodynamics Data Archive (Barker et al. 2021, 2023) and the NASA PDS; Sun and Earth positions from NASA JPL Horizons. NASA does not endorse this game.
credit_line_short: Terrain made from NASA LRO LOLA data (GSFC PGDA / PDS); sky geometry from JPL Horizons.
fields_used: surface height (m) above the 1,737.4 km sphere, south polar stereographic 5/20/40/80 m per pixel
JPL Horizons Sun and Earth azimuth/elevation

aurora.name: Aurora Station (authored outpost) on the Shackleton-de Gerlache connecting ridge
aurora.rule: highest LOLA pixel within 1,500 m of the centre of PGDA Site01 (Connecting ridge, Mazarico et al. 2011 site 1), x = -11,000 m, y = -12,000 m

malapert_summit.name: Malapert relay summit (authored platform at the highest point of Mons Malapert)
malapert_summit.rule: highest LOLA pixel of PGDA Site23 (Malapert massif) within 6,000 m of the USGS/IAU Mons Malapert centre, -85.98 deg, -1.67 deg E

cold_trap.name: Chapter 4 cold trap: a small permanently shadowed basin reached by a ridge road from Aurora
cold_trap.rule: PSR from LPSR_80S_20MPP_ADJ with 0.3 to 6 km2 of area, outside Shackleton, whose slope-limited (<= 12 deg) route from Aurora on the 20 m DEM is closest to 12 km; the site is the lowest PSR pixel

derived.name: aurora_site_height
derived.formula: highest LOLA 5 m pixel within 1.5 km of PGDA Site01 (Connecting ridge) centre
derived.drives: where Aurora stands; exterior scenes LOC-06

derived.name: malapert_summit_height
derived.formula: highest LOLA 5 m pixel within 6 km of the IAU Mons Malapert centre
derived.drives: P-16 why the summit sees Earth; LOC-12

derived.name: cold_trap_psr_area
derived.formula: area of the chosen permanently shadowed region in LPSR_80S_20MPP_ADJ

derived.name: cold_trap_road_length
derived.formula: least-cost road from Aurora on the 20 m DEM with every cell <= 12 deg
derived.drives: P-07 route B (game keeps 12 km / 12 deg)

derived.name: cold_trap_road_max_slope
derived.drives: P-07 slope card (rover limit 15 deg from VIPER)

derived.name: relay_road_length
derived.formula: least-cost road Aurora -> Malapert summit on the 80 m DEM, every cell <= 12 deg
derived.drives: P-15 '120 km each way' (game number unchanged; the real road is longer)

derived.name: relay_road_max_slope
derived.formula: steepest cell on that road; cells over 12 deg are allowed up to the 15 deg VIPER design incline only where no gentler way exists

derived.name: relay_road_length_over_12_deg
derived.formula: length of that road on cells steeper than 12 deg (the summit plateau is ringed by 12-15 deg slopes on the 80 m grid)
derived.drives: P-15 'slope warnings' on the last summit approach

derived.name: aurora_sun_above_terrain_april_2046
derived.formula: hours 10 Apr - 1 May 2046 when the Sun's centre is above the LOLA horizon seen from 2 m at Aurora (Horizons + horizon mask)
derived.drives: P-02 night length context (the 36 h night stays an authored training scenario)

derived.name: aurora_longest_sun_below_terrain_april_2046
derived.formula: longest unbroken run of hours 10 Apr - 1 May 2046 with the Sun's centre behind the terrain seen from 2 m at Aurora; from 2046-04-11T14:00Z to 2046-04-19T15:00Z
derived.drives: science note for P-02: the real ridge point had a longer darkness earlier that month than the authored 36 h night

derived.name: aurora_mast_sun_above_terrain_april_2046
derived.formula: same hours seen from the solar array's lower edge, 10.0 m up (the NASA VSAT relocatable array's blankets span 10-16 m); longest darkness there 85 h
derived.drives: P-02 power context: why Aurora stores energy (Mazarico 2011)

derived.name: earth_elevation_malapert_summit_9_apr_2047
derived.formula: Horizons Earth elevation from the pinned summit at 01:15 UT

derived.name: malapert_terrain_horizon_toward_earth
derived.formula: LOLA terrain horizon at Earth's azimuth from the summit (2 m eye, curvature removed); Earth's centre clears it by 2.30 deg, and in every hour of 8-10 Apr 2047 (73 of 73)
derived.drives: P-16: the real summit sees Earth over the real terrain, which the pole cannot

derived.name: eclipse_12_jan_2047_sun_and_earth_above_aurora_terrain
derived.formula: at 01:00 UT the Sun (el -0.242) and Earth (el -0.159) both clear Aurora's terrain horizon (-3.03 deg toward the Sun)
derived.drives: P-11/P-12 the eclipse is in view from Aurora's ridge (SCIENCE_AND_DATA E20 asked for this check)

boundary: Aurora, the vault shelf and the relay platform are authored places set on real LOLA terrain; the heights, slopes, shadows and Sun/Earth angles are computed from NASA data, the buildings, roads and the 36-hour night are not measurements. Game numbers (12 km, 12 deg, 120 km) stay as in game-design/08_PUZZLE_DESIGNS.md; the computed road lengths are shown beside them, never instead of them.
